ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions list, and the Swiss SECO consolidated financial sanctions (SR 946.203); PEP identification and enhanced due diligence under AMLA Article 6 and FINMA Circular 2020/1; reportable suspicious activity must be filed with the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) pursuant to AMLA Article 9.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Central Business Name Index of Switzerland (https://www.zefix.ch) and the cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the intended seat
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be formed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh), using the Latin script; an Aktiengesellschaft must contain the legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' ('SA' in French); non-Latin script transliterations are not accepted in the Commercial Register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name availability is verified through ZEFIX and reserved by written application to the cantonal Commercial Register Office; one extension of 180 days may be requested before expiry. Upon rejection under OR Articles 944-950, the applicant may file a written objection with the same office within 10 days of notification; if upheld, an administrative appeal to the cantonal administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) must be lodged within 30 days of service; a final appeal lies to the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as an exclusive registered office. OR Article 626 requires a physical registered office address in the seat canton, accessible to authorities and the statutory auditor. Third-party domiciliation services are acceptable provided physical presence and corporate record access are maintained; pure P.O. Box or virtual-only addresses are rejected by the Commercial Register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this standard-risk wholesale profile: approximately 5% to 8% annual probability where a dedicated physical office or licensed domiciliation provider is used; unannounced on-site inspection likelihood increases to 15% to 20% where the address is a flagged cross-border shell or mass domiciliation provider subject to Commercial Register or SECO review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), alternatively Swiss Civil Code (ZGB), Sections 626-640 OR (incorporation, share capital, board duties), Section 641 OR (commercial register), Section 643 OR (articles of association), Section 644 OR (notarial attestation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, administered under the Federal Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (Errichtungsprotokoll und Statuten / Acte constitutif notarié) together with the signed articles of association (Statuten) and the Commercial Register registration application (Handelsregister-Anmeldung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid in cash before registration, deposited with a Swiss bank under a blocked capital confirmation (Sperrkonto) or an escrow/escrow account, and documentation of free availability must be presented to the notary and Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the duly convened First Board Meeting, the Board of Directors resolved: (1) to accept and confirm the subscription of all issued shares in accordance with the notarized articles of association; (2) to designate the registered office at the address stated in the statutory instruments, with the Commercial Register Office as competent public registry; (3) to appoint the persons named in the incorporation file as Chairperson, CEO and authorised officer with individual signature; (4) to authorise these officers to execute all filings, bank mandates and licence applications, including the food business registration; and (5) to declare that the required paid-up capital has been fully funded and is at the free disposal of the company, subject to statutory restrictions. This resolution is adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of Articles of Association and Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonally recognised notary public (Notar / Notaire) relevant to the registered office canton of the Aktiengesellschaft.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory documents, including the articles of association, founders' confirmation, undersigned directors, capital statement, registered office address, and share allocation. Appear before the notary with passport or corporate tax ID for each founder, director and authorised officer. The notary must verify identity, capacity, legality of the business purpose, and the true availability of subscribed capital; then authenticate and sign the deed. For remote founders, a qualified electronic signature or an apostilled power of attorney must be executed. Submit to the notary the final issued share register and a bank confirmation or blocked capital certificate if the deed is being completed before the capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Draft statutory deed and articles of association
Passport or identity card of each founder and director
Certificate of registered address / lease for registered office
Founder's declaration confirming comprehension of corporate law
Power of attorney if signed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the draft, remedy by correcting the registered office description, adjusting the authorised officer list, or filing an amended capital declaration. If statutory requirements are incomplete, the notary will issue a list of defects; execute a supplementary notarial statement and file an amended deed with definitive signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Minimum Paid-In Capital in Blocked Swiss Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g. UBS, Credit Suisse/now UBS, ZKB, Raiffeisen) acting through the corporate account officer and the Capital Deposit / Escrow Desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Swiss bank corporate 'blocked capital' account or a dedicated escrow account for the formed AG. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 of the nominal share capital from disclosed source-of-funds accounts. Execute the bank mandate and the capital deposit agreement (Schuldanerkennung / avoir bloqué) in which the bank confirms that the funds are at the company's free disposal but blocked until the Commercial Register certificate is issued. The bank must issue a capital confirmation letter (Bestätigung der Liberierung) addressed to the notary and the Commercial Register, including depositor name, account number, amount, and blocked status. The confirmation letter must be presented to the notary or registry when filing registration.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
Bank account application and corporate due-diligence forms
Passport/identity of directors and beneficial owners
Statement of source of funds
Draft articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for enhanced due diligence, produce enhanced source-of-wealth evidence or transfer the funds via a parent bank in Switzerland. If the account is not established, apply at another cantonal bank or fintech corporate payment provider holding full banking licence. Should the capital confirmation show an amount below CHF 50,000, top up the deposit and request a revised certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application and Electronic Registration Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office canton, through the e-register platform (eService / eHandelsregister) or by paper application with legalised document packet.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the publication-type application to the Commercial Register, attaching: the notarised deed and articles of association, bank capital confirmation, board members' acceptance and signature specimen cards (Schriftprobe), and any necessary consent statement from the cantonal authorities if the business purpose requires a licence (food wholesaling). Provide the statutory corporate information: legal form 'Aktiengesellschaft', trade name, registered office, main purpose, share capital CHF 100,000, number of shares, board members with individual or collective signature, and auditors if applicable. After the registry reviews and confirms the application, pay the cantonal publication fee. The Commercial Register then appoints a judge or clerk for final review and creates the registration entry.
required_dossiers: Notarised incorporation deed and Statuten
Bank capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung)
First board resolution and officer signature specimen cards (Schriftprobe bei der Amtsperson)
Passport copies of all board members
Mandate from the CEO / chairperson if filed by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or interim deficiency, counsel will address the specific objection and file a corrective application within 60 days where allowed. Missing signature specimens are cured by a personal appearance at the registry; if the notarised deed lacks a mandatory clause, the notary issues a supplemental declaration to rectify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Tax Administration, Social Security and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (Steueramt / Administration fiscale cantonale), Federal Department of Finance (FDF) for VAT matters, and the cantonal compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/IV/EO and unemployment insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Commercial Register excerpt and the certificate of incorporation (Handelsregisterauszug), file the definitive application with the cantonal tax office to obtain the tax number and confirmation of local tax domicile. Simultaneously apply for the employer social-security number with the cantonal compensation fund and register the company with the Federal Social Insurance Compensation Fund if the payroll worker is hired, and provide the wage list for accident insurance (SUVA or private accident insurer). For VAT, file the VAT registration form to the Federal Taxation Administration as the company expects supplies for export with input VAT deduction purposes. Provide the earnings information, balance sheet, and trade description. Once tax numbers are received, update the bank mandate and pay invoices accordingly.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt post-registration
Articles of association
Confirmation of registered office and actual business opening
Directors' passport and residence permit for board member
Wage and remuneration declaration for social insurance
VAT registration form if exempt or export status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide the audited share capital statement. If the compensation fund marks a backlog, apply for a provisional certificate. Tax and social security registrations can be administratively corrected without penalty if filed within 30 days of the deficiency notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Food Business and Sectoral Licence Notification with Cantonal Food Control
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Food Safety Authority (Kantonale Lebensmittelkontrolle / Service de consommation et affaires vétérinaires) and the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV/FSVO). Operating authority for public guidance is the municipality where the wholesale warehouse is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal incorporation, file the food business notification to the competent cantonal food-control authority, presenting the planned activity 'wholesale, storage and international bulk distribution of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals'. Submit a declaration covering storage conditions, packaging, traceability, HACCP capacity, organic certificate if the goods will be sold as organic, and the selected control body. Obtain the operating licence / registration number for the warehouse and review if a dedicated cantonal food permit is needed for handling foods of plant origin. If exports to non-EU markets are intended, the company may additionally submit a statement of responsibility to the FSVO for phytosanitary and pollutant control standards.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register partial excerpt confirming entity and purpose
Food business notification form of the canton
Description of warehouse / cold storage inventory
Traceability and recall plan
Organic certificate or organic operator registration if applicable
Third-party pest-control and hygiene service contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the cantonal food authority requests inspection, agree to a pre-vetting visit within 2 weeks and comply with corrective action against pest evidence; if the notification is considered incomplete, amend the specific exposure description and submit the revised operational plan. Appeal through cantonal administrative remedy within 20 days from adverse notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit / Direction du travail, de l'immigration et de la formation professionnelle) together with the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO, BLV) for food-sector controls
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operation Licence for wholesale and warehouse storage of dried botanicals / foodstuffs, issued pursuant to the Foodstuffs Act (Lebensmittelgesetz) and the Foodstuffs Importation Regulation; additionally, for export destinations requiring an industrial food-processing permit, a cantonal manufacturing operating permit might be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU), Environment Section of the Canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / ex-post notification only under the Ordinance on Environmental Impact Assessment (UVPV); a full EIA report is not required for a wholesale and dry storage facility without processing, coating, or substantial solvent use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) and the Ordinance on Waste (VVEA) for any condensate or cleaning wastewater; no VOC emission exceedance expected from dried-goji rehydration/packaging, but if any coating or fumigation occurs, maintain thresholds under Annex 2 of the Ordinance on Air Pollution (LRV) and report to the cantonal air authorities. For all waste, use licensed disposal routes and retain manifests for non-hazardous organic residues, compost and packaging waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Feuerpolizeiliche Nutzungsbewilligung) issued by the cantonal Fire Prevention Inspectorate, including fire-protection compartmentation of the storage area, hydrant and extinguisher layout, loading dock lane safety, and electrical installation certificate. Structural load inspection of warehouse racks/storage heights by a recognised civil engineer in accordance with cantonal construction codes must be filed. Occupational clearance is mandatory under the Federal Ordinance on Accident Prevention (VUV), with a low-risk warehouse declaration to the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA) or an approved private occupational insurer, confirming statutory accident-insurance coverage for employees, ergonomic handling instruction for pallet movement, and audible/fire-exit signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenoessische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration federale des contributions (AFC) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA); VAT Main Division, Schwarztorstrasse 25, 3003 Bern; central UID (business identification) register portal at www.uid.ch; official e-services portal at www.estv.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft obtains its Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID-CH) ex officio upon entry in the Cantonal Commercial Register; the UID-CH simultaneously serves as the Swiss VAT ID (MWST-Nr.). A foreign entity without a Swiss commercial register entry must apply to the ESTV VAT Main Division for a UID-CH and VAT registration before performing taxable supplies if cumulative worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Non-resident applicants must appoint a Swiss service address and, in practice, a Swiss fiscal representative; a non-resident exporter with no Swiss nexus and no domestic taxable supplies has no Swiss VAT registration obligation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Swiss AG is a separate corporate taxpayer subject to direct federal tax (8.5% statutory rate on net profit; approximately 4.33% effective after pro-rata relief), cantonal and communal profit taxes, net wealth tax on equity, and Swiss VAT on taxable supplies. Residence-based worldwide taxation applies, tempered by the situ-territoire principle exempting foreign permanent establishment profits and foreign immovable property; pass-through or check-the-box treatment is not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Swiss law. Available elections relevant to an AG exporter: (i) group VAT unit election (Steuergruppe / unite fiscale) for economically integrated Swiss entities; (ii) participation exemption / reduction (Beteiligungsabzug) election on qualifying dividend and capital gain income; (iii) cantonal notional interest deduction (NID) in participating cantons; (iv) election of the Swiss VAT reporting period (quarterly, semi-annual or annual); (v) small-business category election with renunciation of input VAT deduction; (vi) election to treat the AG as a holding company under cantonal holding status principles only for older tax regimes (grandfathered cases); (vii) option to claim foreign PE income exemption under the ordinary exemption method.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Federal Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / VAT) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG / LTVA), administered by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (exclusive of exempt supplies and real estate sale costs) triggers mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. Enhanced thresholds apply to certain categories: CHF 250,000 for donation-collecting non-profits and CHF 150,000 for agricultural and healthcare activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API filing, or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary for B2B and public-sector exchange uses the SwissPeppol (eBill/Peppol BIS) standard; the Swiss QR-bill is mandatory for all payment slips issued to Swiss residents from 1 July 2020. Invoices must satisfy the statutory content requirements of Art. 26a of the VAT Ordinance in any format or medium, with a 10-year electronic archiving obligation for all export substantiation records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies where the supplier proves, with export documentation, that goods were physically removed from Swiss territory (or from a Swiss customs free zone) to a foreign destination for a foreign-domiciled buyer or a foreign permanent establishment of a Swiss entity. Directly related transport, logistics, commission, and packaging services provided in connection with the export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals equally qualify for 0%. The supplier must receive the consideration from the foreign buyer and retain a coherent file demonstrating the commercial identity of goods, the dispatch route, and the foreign recipient. Qualifying export transactions preserve the full input VAT deduction and are reported in the periodic Swiss VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated customs export declaration (ARD / Ausfuhrdeklaration lodged via GemDat) or transit and end-use customs documentation for removals from customs bonded warehouses
Commercial invoice with HS tariff classification and Incoterms for dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, including the foreign consignee details
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR international consignment note evidencing the physical border crossing
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank transfer credit confirmation showing receipt of foreign consideration in the Swiss settlement account
Packing list and phytosanitary certificate demonstrating botanical identity and compliance with food or herbal supplement export controls
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV audit and refund units examine export zero-ratings for formal dossier completeness and economic substance, including the reality of the foreign buyer and the Swiss bank receipt. Deficiencies trigger reclassification as a domestic taxable supply at 8.1% VAT, plus default interest of 4.5%-5% per annum; tax omission penalties reach up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 175 MWSTG). Fraudulent zero-rating schemes attract criminal fines and potential imprisonment, with assessment limitation periods of 5 years for negligent omissions and 10 years for intentional evasion or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the Federal Department of Finance (FDF), with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) coordinating cross-border financia affairs
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) on both current and capital account. There are no exchange controls, no licensing requirements, and no restrictions on the repatriation of share capital, dividends, interest, or trade proceeds. The Capital Account is fully open for non-resident investors, and the current account is unrestricted. Profit remittance is subject only to standard Swiss withholding tax of 35% on dividends unless reduced by treaty or participation relief; no additional cantonal or federal gates apply. Non-resident shareholders may freely hold and transfer AG shares, subject to entry into the Swiss commercial register for qualified participations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements and no mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts in any currency may be retained offshore, converted at freely negotiated market rates, or held in domestic multi-currency accounts. Receipts should be documented in the Swiss customs electronic export declaration system (NCTS) and in the company's statutory accounts; Swiss GAAP requires accrual recognition at the spot exchange rate at transaction date.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI entities are not authorised banking institutions under Swiss law and cannot open resident operational bank accounts in Switzerland. They are only viable for auxiliary payment processing, not for the primary liquidity or escrow rail. Swiss FINMA-licensed fintech companies (e.g., bank-like payment firms under the Fintech Licence regime) may hold client funds up to CHF 100 million on interest-bearing accounts, but they do not provide commercial credit or documentary credit facilities. Foreign EMIs such as UK-licensed or EU-passporting EMIs may clear CHF only through Swiss SIX-member banks, exposing the principal to ring-fenced counterparty risk. Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury account; Medium as an ancillary low-value collection channel for non-core markets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all directors is not an absolute statutory requirement. Swiss banks are permitted to complete identity verification via a recognised video-identification process (FINMA Circular 2016/07 and OBA-FINMA) provided that the video call is real-time, the identification document is checked with chip-reading or equivalent technical means, and the film is retained. However, many tier-1 banks still require at least one in-person meeting with the economic beneficiary or a senior officer at a Swiss branch, embassy annex, or trusted corresponding bank for the first account for complex cross-border structures. For the CH_AG with non-resident directors and an export business to high-intensity markets, a physical onboarding interview in Zurich or Geneva is strongly recommended to avoid underwriting delays, but remote opening remains legally permissible for standard low-risk wholesale clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity if the AG is owned through opaque foreign holding structures or discretionary trusts without full UBO disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart signed by all shareholders; Swiss commercial register excerpt; notarised UBO registry declaration; extract from the foreign ultimate parent's registry; audited statutory accounts; written confirmation of capital source; notarised signatures and powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty exposure when channeling exports of herbal botanicals to jurisdictions outside FATF reciprocal cooperation or with enhanced monitoring status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Referenced commercial agreements with end-buyers; documentary evidence of underlying trade (pro-forma invoices, bills of lading, weight and quality certificates); third-party sanctions screening reports; certificate of origin; phytosanitary certificate; Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) or Swissmedic classification letter; bank-verified purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth concerns due to rapid capital injection from non-resident investors into a newly formed AG without prior banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving capital payment and account mandate; bank statement from the sending banking institution; source-of-wealth file including tax returns, audited financial statements, real estate ownership deeds, notes on liquidation of other assets; tax clearance certificate from the country of residence; confirmation of deposit of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital with full legal capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cash-like settlement expectations or atypical payment routing through third-party jurisdictions with no commercial nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade cycle documentation from factory to port to buyer; corporate packing and logistic contracts; letters of assignment for freight forwarding; bank reference letters; customer due diligence file for each recurring buyer; FX hedging confirmation demonstrating economic exposure; independent audit trail of customs declarations (NCTS).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders may inject capital via SWIFT wire in CHF, EUR, or USD into the AG's capital escrow account at a Swiss tier-1 bank. There is no exchange control approval; the bank will request the SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) to state 'Contribuzione Capitale' or 'Capital Contribution' and may require a copy of the notarised capital payment instruction. For CHF transfers, the rail is SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) operated by SIX Interbank Clearing. EUR transfers use SEPA or SWIFT; USD transfers use correspondent banks via CHIPS or Fedwire. The bank will verify that the sending institution holds a valid SWIFT BIC and that the source of funds corresponds to the UBO declaration. The account should be flagged as 'Capital Escrow' until the commercial register confirms the share capital increase, after which the account can be automatically transmuted into the operational account. The bank will provide a payment acceptance certificate (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) for regulatory evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For open-account terms, the company issues SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers to international suppliers through the SIC/SEPA or correspondent banking network. For confirmed documentary transactions, commercial letters of credit must follow UCP 600, with the issuing bank opening an MT700 and the Swiss beneficiery presenting compliance documents through the confirming bank. For bulk shipments of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, the recommended rail is a sight or deferred documentary LC with a Swiss confirming bank, ensuring that payment occurs against presentation of a clean bill of lading, phytosanitary inspection, certificate of origin, and an organic certification with correct harmonised system codes. For intra-Swiss payments, QR-bill or ISO 20022 payment instructions via SIC are standard. The company may also use SWIFT MT101 for bulk payment initiation from the treasury workstation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards in CHF/EUR/USD offered by Swiss banks (up to 24-36 months maturity without restriction)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic emerging-market currencies via Swiss or international counterparties, provided the underlying is a genuine commercial exposure
Cross-currency basis swaps (XCCY) between CHF and EUR or CHF and USD for balance-sheet hedging of long-term trade finance liabilities
Currency options (call/put) and collars for hedging inwards commodity purchase commitments and outbound sales in hard currency
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps of principal and interest under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Swiss bank or EU counterparty, fully permitted absent speculative purpose

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary annual shareholders' meeting with approval of annual financial statements, appropriation of profits, and discharge of board members; executed meeting minutes must be retained.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders in accordance with Swiss Code of Obligations Arts. 698-699; minutes maintained in corporate minute book.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date / financial year-end, per CO Art. 699(3).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directorial breach of duty and civil liability; shareholder may compel the board to convene a meeting through court order; persistent failure to maintain valid corporate organisation exposes the company to commercial-register dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return, including statutory annual accounts, tax-compliant balance sheet reconciliation, and shareholder declarations required by cantonal and federal tax forms.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the seat canton and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) in coordinated assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Canton-dependent, generally 31 March of the following year for calendar-year companies; electronic filings often receive automatic extensions into the second quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest from the due date; procedural fines; tax penalty up to 30% of evaded tax; criminal sanctions for intentional tax evasion; non-filing leads to enforcement and ultimately commercial-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic VAT settlement: quarterly returns are the standard rule, with annual VAT returns available for eligible taxpayers granted annual settlement by the Federal Tax Administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT Division, through electronic VAT filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each reporting period; annual settlement follows the approved annual period and statutory deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; VAT evasion penalties may reach three times the evaded tax; criminal referral for wilful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial register compliance review: the board of directors documents that registered office, registered share capital, directors, signatory powers, statutory registers, and beneficial-owner records are complete and accurate; no filing is required if no changes occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt); electronic filings made only upon relevant corporate changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty with a documented board review at least annually before the shareholders' meeting and immediately after any material change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative coercive fines for failure to make required filings; inaccurate declarations may attract penal liability; a company with no valid registered office or management after notice is subject to ex officio judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: If ordinary statutory audit applies: audited annual financial statements and audit report, with annual accounts deposited for publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce where required by law.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB); audit report presented to shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited accounts must be approved by shareholders within six months after year-end; publication/deposit obligations apply on the schedule fixed by commercial-register regulations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete ordinary statutory audit or to comply with publication obligations is a regulatory offence subject to fines and administrative enforcement; continued non-compliance may trigger commercial-register strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit under CO Art. 727 applies if two of the following three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive business years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million; gross sales above CHF 40 million; annual average workforce above 250 full-time equivalents. Ordinary audit is also mandatory for licensed, listed, and debenture-issuing companies. All other AGs require limited audit under CO Art. 727a unless exempted by having fewer than 10 full-time equivalents on annual average and unanimous shareholder consent to opt out.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations financial reporting principles (CO Arts. 958a-958f), supported by Swiss GAAP FER for a true-and-fair view; IFRS is permitted for private AGs and mandatory for listed or FINMA-regulated companies. Annual accounts are presented in Swiss francs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not impose a public annual UBO filing for a private AG. The company must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners under CO Art. 697j and a current share register at the registered office. On every share transfer, the board must record the new ownership and beneficial-owner details; before the annual general meeting the board confirms that the registers are current and presents them upon demand to tax authorities, auditors, and financial intermediaries.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienregister) and Beneficial Owner Register under CO Art. 697j
Register of Directors and Authorized Signatories
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300-4,500 per year (CHF 1,200-4,000) for registered office, corporate secretarial support, and registered-agent administration.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500-14,000 for a limited statutory audit of a small export AG; ordinary statutory audits generally range from USD 18,000-40,000 depending on cross-border complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on after-tax profit (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal + cantonal + communal effective rate for a Zug-headquartered AG approximates 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief (100% deduction of qualifying dividend income at federal and cantonal levels); mandatory cantonal patent/IP box granting up to 90% exemption of qualifying net IP income; cantonal R&D super-deduction of up to 50%; optional notional interest deduction on excess equity (available in Zug); reduced capital tax burden for holding and mixed companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal/cantonal corporate income tax return for legal persons (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale des personnes morales) filed through the domicile canton's electronic filing portal (Zug: TaxZug e-portal); the cantonal assessment authority administers both the cantonal tax and the federal direct tax (Art. 105-107 DBG, Art. 120 StHG).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year AGs must file by 30 June of the following year. Written extension requests of one to three months are generally granted by the Zug tax administration; a non-calendar fiscal year requires prior approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wholesale turnover from sales of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, net of trade discounts and returns, before deduction of cost of goods sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No entry by the non-resident shareholder; the Swiss AG alone is assessed. Sales to related foreign distributors must be supported by arm's length invoices and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax per the audited statutory annual financial statements (Swiss GAAP FER / Art. 958-963 OR); the starting point for all tax reconciliation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders cannot offset their own losses against the Swiss AG's profit; only Swiss-source and Switzerland-attributable income is assessed at this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 100% deduction of net dividend income from qualifying participations of at least 10% of nominal capital or CHF 1 million book value, held for 12 months or longer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent shareholders must supply audited shareholding schedules and prove the 10%/CHF 1 million threshold upon request; treaty-resident parents need a current Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year tax losses within the statutory seven-year carryforward window, computed consistently with Art. 67 DBG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforwards are entity-specific and non-transferable; a change in non-resident beneficial ownership exceeding 50% may forfeit the carryforward under the empty-shell anti-abuse practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year-end taxable equity (share capital plus open reserves, after adjustments for non-business assets and participation holdings) forming the base of cantonal and municipal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity contributed by non-resident shareholders is fully taxable capital in Switzerland; shareholder loan balances in excess of thin-capitalization safe harbors are recharacterized as taxable equity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG), default interest at 4.5% p.a. on the assessed federal tax, and a best-judgment estimated assessment by the tax authority; repeated non-filing escalates to tax evasion penalties of up to 150% of evaded tax (first offense) and up to 300% (relapse), plus additional cantonal surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on all dividend distributions, constructive dividends and similar distributions by the Swiss AG (Art. 4 VStG).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must submit a refund claim to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on Form 82 within three years after the calendar year of distribution, attaching an original Tax Residency Certificate, proof of beneficial ownership and audited evidence of the qualifying holding (generally >=10%). Under the Switzerland-China DTA, the WHT on dividends is reduced to 5% for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital, and 10% for portfolio investors; for recurring distributions, an ESTV-approved relief-at-source arrangement (Form 823) may be used to avoid the withhold-and-refund cycle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Swiss withholding tax (Switzerland does not tax outbound royalties at source); treaty rates are commonly 0% to 5%. Interest: 0% statutory WHT on ordinary bank and intercompany loan interest; the 35% WHT applies only to interest on taxable bonds and money-market instruments (Art. 4 VStG); most DTAs, including the Switzerland-China DTA, cap interest WHT at 10%, with several modern treaties providing 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for Swiss groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million; Master File and Local File preparation follows OECD standards where cross-border related-party transactions of the AG exceed approximately CHF 10 million annually (no codified Swiss statutory threshold, but documentation must be contemporaneous and produced on ESTV demand).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations as in other holding jurisdictions, but the substance-over-form doctrine and OECD BEPS minimum standards apply strictly: the AG must maintain real business premises, qualified local employees, active management and decision-making in Switzerland, and Swiss bank accounts; letterbox entities are denied treaty benefits under the MLI/PPT, face recharacterization of income as constructive dividends (Art. 21 VStG), and risk revocation of the statutory wholesale authorization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Tax Fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of dried goji berry export revenue, use of inflated purchase invoices from related herbal suppliers, or concealment of foreign bank accounts from the assessing tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 175 DBG: fine of up to 1.5 times the evaded federal tax for a first offense and up to 3 times for a repeat offense, plus default interest at 4.5% p.a.; tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG carries imprisonment of up to five years and additional fines; the unpaid tax remains fully collectible and cantonal penalties apply in parallel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and signatories who knowingly caused the under-declaration face criminal conviction, passport seizure and travel bans under the Swiss Code of Criminal Procedure, removal from the commercial register, and civil restitution claims by the tax administration and creditors under Art. 754 OR; culpable participation also triggers anti-money-laundering reporting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Verrechnungssteuer (35% WHT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or other distributable benefits to foreign or domestic shareholders without deducting the statutory 35% anticipatory tax at source, or filing incomplete withholding tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AG is jointly and severally liable for the grossed-up unpaid WHT (Art. 14 VStG), compounded with 4.5% default interest (Art. 13 VStG) and a procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 60 VStG); the WHT claim enjoys statutory priority in bankruptcy and any under-withholding on benefits-in-kind is reclassified as a further taxable distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who ordered or tolerated unauthorized distributions are personally liable for the shortfall; culpable violation of the WHT obligation is a crime under Art. 62 VStG punishable by imprisonment of up to three years, and the administration may sue directors directly for restitution of the uncollected amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Hidden Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dried goji berry inventory to a related foreign trader at non-arm's-length margins, paying excessive management fees to a related intermediary in Hong Kong or Mainland China, or failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Profit correction under Art. 57-58 DBG raising the taxable profit at the effective Zug rate of about 11.9%, reclassification of the shifted amount as a constructive dividend subject to 35% WHT plus 4.5% interest, penalty of up to 1.5 times the additional tax, and denial of corresponding relief under MAP/APA procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certified false transfer pricing documentation or instructed external advisors to prepare misleading benchmarks are criminally exposed under Art. 186 DBG and become personally liable for the uncollectible tax under Art. 218 DBG in case of company insolvency; professional advisors face license and disciplinary sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-Company Substance Deficiency and AML Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a letterbox with no local premises, staff or decision-making; misrepresenting the beneficial owner of the goji berry trading entity; failing customer due diligence and AML controls on Swift-TT/wire payment rails; or transacting with sanctioned or opaque herbal-supply counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits and domestic deductions under the MLI/PPT anti-abuse rules, retroactive reclassification of accumulated profit as a 35% WHT-charged constructive dividend, revocation of the wholesale food and botanical license under the Swiss Foodstuffs Act, AML fines of up to CHF 500,000 (Art. 37 AMLA) with higher FINMA enforcement measures, imprisonment of up to three years under Art. 305bis StGB, and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal money-laundering convictions with imprisonment and fines at the same scale, travel restrictions and asset freezes during investigation, disqualification from future board service, and joint and several civil liability to the company, tax authorities and wronged third parties under Art. 754 OR.
